reason: The CIAAW CSV gives 28.9815(1) for aluminium in 1969. Aluminium is 26.9815 in the 1961 row and 26.981 54(1) in the 1971 row of the same file, and 28.98 would place it above silicon (28.08); the leading digit is taken as a transcription slip. Checked against the 1969 report (Pure Appl. Chem. 21, 91 (1970), doi:10.1351/pac197021010091): Table XIV (p. 105) and Table XV (p. 106) both print aluminium as 26.9815 (decimal point printed as a raised dot) with footnote a (mononuclidic element) and the last digit in normal type, which the tables define as reliable to ±1 in the last digit, so 26.9815(1) is the printed value.
